identity.life_stage: married, five children, school cafeteria manager

engagement.interaction_backstory: She feeds six hundred children a day and comes home to five of her own, and the house runs on music from four o'clock onward. She found the Latin worship catalog and heard traditions from both sides of the river treated as equals, which she has never seen on an English-language site.

depth.core_contradiction: Feeds everybody and eats standing up at the counter.
depth.wound: Her oldest crossed a line at nineteen and there was a year nobody in the family will describe.
depth.longing: All five of them at the same table without anybody watching the door.
depth.faith_journey: Catholic, Guadalupana, the whole calendar; her faith is her mother's and she has never wanted a different one.
depth.voice_fingerprint: "Mija" to everyone including men her own age; laughs before delivering bad news.
depth.open_doubt: Whether the year of prayer worked or the boy just got tired.

social_graph.note: drives a route; home late; steady
23; back home; they do not talk about it

depth.emotional_weather_default: Warm and busy; quiet on the drive to work.
depth.daily_texture: Cafeteria at 5:30, six hundred trays, the house at four, rosary in the car.
depth.sensory_anchor: The Guadalupe hymn sung at 5am on the twelfth of December by a whole neighborhood.
depth.living_arc: Learning to let the oldest be an adult, badly and slowly.
